# M2-2: MCP server in serve

- Milestone: M2
- Branch / worktree: `t/M2-2`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M2-2`
- Depends on: M2-1b
- Touches (exclusive while running): mcp/ (new), cmd/, config/, .env.example, go.mod, go.sum
- Plan refs: §4 (all), N6, N7, R9. Spike: `spikes/mcp/{main,mcpserver}.go`.
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (the endpoint stays dark until M2-5)

## Goal
`finbot serve` runs an authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP server beside the scheduler, with the first read tool. Tools read
SQLite only and never call YNAB, so they can't touch the rate budget.

## Scope
- `mcp/`: go-sdk v1.8.0, resource-server auth using the `auth/` verifier. `tools/list` is limited by the caller's token.
- Set the protected-resource metadata `ResourceName` to exactly `finbot` (the spike says `finbot (spike)`). M2-5 uses this to prove traffic left the spike.
- Mount the AS with `mux.Handle("/oauth/", srv)` and `mux.Handle("/.well-known/", srv)`. Set `RequireBearerTokenOptions.Scopes` to `[]string{auth.ScopeMCP}`, because `VerifyToken` doesn't check scope itself.
- Port the spike's `cors` and `logRequests` middleware from `spikes/mcp/main.go`. Browser clients need `cors`. Logs stay free of tokens, emails and ids.
- Tool registration: one slice in `mcp/`, with each tools file adding itself, so later tasks only add files.
- Tool `data_freshness`. A shared response helper puts data freshness in every tool response (§4).
- Config: `MCP_LISTEN_ADDR` (default `:8080`), `MCP_PUBLIC_URL`, `MCP_DATA_DIR` only if still needed,
  `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS`. MCP is disabled unless all the required
  values are set, so existing deploys and local runs keep working.
- **Health stays private.** The tunnel forwards every path on the MCP port to the public internet, and `/healthz` returns
  `last_error`. Serve it on its own listener: `HTTP_ADDR` default becomes `127.0.0.1:8081`, and the MCP port must return
  404 for `/healthz`. `finbot health` keeps working from inside the container, and `cmd/probe.go`'s default moves to match.
- `finbot revoke <email | u_hash | --all>`: one-step revocation via `RevokeUser`, no restart. The hash form means no email needs to be on argv in a container exec. It opens only `FINBOT_DB_PATH` and needs no YNAB or Google env.
- Add `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` to `secrets(cfg)` in `cmd/app.go`.
- Run `auth.Prune` at startup and daily, on the scheduler's goroutine, logging its outcome. A failure must not fail the sync.
- Graceful shutdown covers the new listener. Logs carry no tokens, emails or ids.
- If finbot logs client IPs, use `CF-Connecting-IP` only as §4 allows.

## Out of scope
- Other tools (M2-3, M2-4), compose, tunnel and deploy.sh (M2-5), write tools (M5).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Test: `/mcp` without a token returns 401 with resource metadata; with a valid token `tools/list` and
      `data_freshness` work; with a revoked token returns 401.
- [ ] Test: a request with the public Host on the `:8080` listener isn't refused by the DNS-rebinding guard.
- [ ] Test: `/healthz` is 404 on the MCP listener and works on `HTTP_ADDR`; `finbot health` exits 0.
- [ ] Test: serve with MCP config blank behaves as today (sync, status and backup jobs run, no MCP listener).
- [ ] Test: `finbot revoke` works with only `FINBOT_DB_PATH` set.
- [ ] Test: the protected-resource metadata has `ResourceName` `finbot`.
- [ ] Test: `Prune` runs at startup and on its tick, and a Prune error doesn't mark sync unhealthy.
- [ ] Test: a token without the MCP scope is refused on `/mcp`; a browser preflight gets the CORS headers.
- [ ] Test: SIGTERM closes both listeners and the DB.
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green
